says: Decision 0555 bans vi.mock, vi.doMock, vi.spyOn and vi.stubEnv in next/ and our tooling and says the ban is held at zero by oxlint's vitest/no-restricted-vi-methods, but that rule is not set in .oxlintrc.json (only the vitest plugin is on, at line 6), and 41 files under next/ still call the banned methods, so the code lags the decision. The approved plans that already carry this work are the folder plans docs/plan/quests/mock-oxlint-plugins-PLAN.md, mock-node-PLAN.md, mock-node-dev-PLAN.md, mock-cloudflare-PLAN.md and mock-app-src-PLAN.md (with their sibling mock-*-PLAN.md files), each of which adds its folder's vitest/no-restricted-vi-methods block and fixes that folder's calls. Ticket text: land those approved mock plans, and do not plan the work again; each sets vitest/no-restricted-vi-methods with the messages 0555 gives for its folder and fixes the calls with test layers, a Config provider and the Recorder as 0555 says, never with a list of leftovers (0524).
proof: `grep -c 'no-restricted-vi-methods' .oxlintrc.json` prints 0; `rg -l '\bvi\.(mock|doMock|spyOn|stubEnv)\(' --glob '!node_modules' next | wc -l` prints 41 files, and `rg -o` on the same pattern finds 119 calls (mock 43, doMock 9, spyOn 44, stubEnv 23).
cost: Nothing stops a new banned call, and the cleanup 0555 describes cannot be proved done, so the stand-ins that come from the test framework instead of a service layer keep growing.
